summary: This CSS stylesheet styles code snippet components with language-specific branding. It creates a consistent dark code display area, a collapsible toolbar with language logos and brand colors, and optional line-by-line annotations (ELI5 mode). The key innovation is that each language now declares a single --lang-color variable that drives the toolbar underline, logo color, and focus ring, rather than repeating the color across multiple rules.

explanations.42: The 'composes' syntax (from CSS Modules) means this class inherits all the styles from the 'mk-surface' class defined elsewhere, then adds its own rules on top.
explanations.74: The :last-child selector targets the very last element inside .snippet_inner and removes its bottom margin so it doesn't create extra spacing at the end.
explanations.80: The :has(pre) selector checks if this element contains a <pre> tag anywhere inside it; if so, removes the padding because the <pre> will provide its own.
explanations.94: The !important flag forces these background colors to transparent, overriding any background colors that Prism (the syntax highlighter) or other libraries tried to set.
explanations.108: This uses rgba() with four values: red, green, blue, and alpha (transparency). The 0.06 means 6% opaque white over the dark background.
explanations.125: This sets a CSS custom property (variable) that starts at 0 degrees; it will be changed to 180 degrees when the button opens to rotate the chevron icon.
explanations.137: The comma after var(--lang-color, var(--mk-primary)) provides a fallback: if --lang-color isn't defined on this element, use --mk-primary instead.
explanations.164: This applies the rotation value stored in --chevron-rotation to the chevron element; the transition on line 163 makes it animate smoothly over 0.3 seconds.
explanations.186: This calculates the max height by taking the number of lines to show, multiplying by line-height (1.6) and font size (0.85rem), then adding padding. It ensures the peek window cuts between lines, not through text.
explanations.199: This creates a fade effect at the bottom: starts transparent at the top and becomes the code background color by 85% down, signaling there's more content below.
explanations.271: If --lang-color isn't defined on the element, fall back to --mk-n-500 (a neutral gray), so logos always have a color even without a language-specific class.
explanations.282: This adds a subtle dark shadow to light-colored logos so they're visible against the light sand-colored toolbar without changing the actual brand color.
explanations.300: This is the base rule for all variant classes: set a default neutral color and a 3px colored border on top, which any specific language class can override.
explanations.422: border-radius: 0 0 ... means the top corners are sharp (0 radius) but the bottom corners are rounded using the --mk-radius-md variable.
explanations.439: white-space: pre preserves all whitespace and line breaks exactly as written, preventing the browser from collapsing multiple spaces into one.
explanations.471: This uses rgba with green channel (147), blue channel (183), red channel (100), and alpha 0.14; it creates a subtle green tint for the badge background.
explanations.523: :where() removes the specificity that this selector would normally add, so the button's own :hover rule on line 512 always wins when you hover over it.
explanations.536: min(270px, 90vw) returns whichever is smaller: 270 pixels or 90% of the viewport width, so the tooltip shrinks on mobile without getting cut off.
explanations.548: translateY moves the tooltip up by its own height (100%) plus 8 pixels of gap, positioning it above the badge.
